French high wire artist Philippe Petit balances at the edge of one of the World Trade Center Towers. New York City. 1986.

Philippe Petit (born 13 August 1949) is a French high-wire artist who gained fame for his high-wire walk between the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City on August 7, 1974. This stunt was documented in the Academy Award winning film Man on Wire. Pictures may be seen here.

For his unauthorized feat 1,350 feet (400 metres) above the ground, he rigged a 450-pound (200-kilogram) cable and used a custom-made 26-foot (8-metre) long, 55-pound (25-kilogram) balancing pole. He performed for 45 minutes, making eight passes along the wire. All charges against him were dismissed in exchange for his doing a performance in Central Park for children.

The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey later gave Petit a lifetime pass to the Twin Towers' Observation Deck. As may be seen in this photograph, he autographed a steel beam close to the point where he began his walk.
